Figure 3 illustrates the expenditures for R&D and innovation (in BGN) across various sectors of the national economy over a specified period. The chart employs a line graph format with multiple colored lines, each representing a different sector, plotted against a shared horizontal and vertical axis.

The horizontal axis (X-axis) represents the time period, labeled with discrete, equally spaced tick marks corresponding to years. The specific years marked on the axis are 2003, 2005, 2007, 2009, 2011, 2013, 2015, 2017, and 2019. The axis is linear and lacks explicit numerical values or units between the labeled years, indicating that the intervals are annual. The vertical axis (Y-axis) represents expenditure in Bulgarian Lev (BGN), with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 200,000. The axis is marked with labeled tick intervals at 0, 5,000, 10,000, 15,000, and 20,000.

The chart contains five distinct lines, each with a unique color and corresponding to a specific economic sector as indicated by the legend:
- A solid orange line represents “Agriculture, forestry, and fishing.”
- A solid gray line represents “Manufacturing.”
- A solid yellow line represents “Repair of motor vehicles and motorcycles.”
- A solid blue line represents “Creation and dissemination of information and theoretical products; educational services.”
- A solid brown line represents “Other services.”

The “Agriculture, forestry, and fishing” line (orange) remains near the baseline, fluctuating slightly above 0, with values approximately between 0 and 5,000 BGN throughout the period.

The “Manufacturing” line (gray) begins near 5,000 BGN, dips slightly, then rises steadily to approximately 15,000 BGN by 2013, followed by a sharp increase to around 17,000 BGN by 2015, and then plateaus near 20,000 BGN through 2019.

The “Repair of motor vehicles and motorcycles” line (yellow) starts near 0, rises slightly to around 2,000 BGN by 2007, then remains relatively flat near 0 until 2013, after which it rises to approximately 5,000 BGN by 2019.

The “Creation and dissemination of information and theoretical products; educational services” line (blue) begins near 0, rises gradually to approximately 5,000 BGN by 2009, then increases sharply to around 10,000 BGN by 2013, followed by a further steep rise to approximately 15,000 BGN by 2015, and then levels off near 17,000 BGN through 2019.

The “Other services” line (brown) is nearly flat and consistently near 0 BGN across the entire period.
